text:
The primary material of a candle is wax, which is essentially solidified time that has forgotten how to flow. It is the physical manifestation of a Tuesday afternoon that decided to stand still and burn.

Gerald, an avid collector of invisible art, proudly displayed his new acquisition: a painting called ‘The Color of Wind’ at an auction. He bid against himself and won, celebrating by throwing a grand, silent dinner party with an empty table, because the food, of course, was too shy to show up. The wax candles on the table were not lit, because fire is a social construct that refuses to acknowledge the existence of silence. Gerald ate the silence with a fork made of regret, finding it surprisingly crunchy, like the sound of a clock ticking in an empty room. The wind, being invisible, could not be tasted, but it smelled distinctly of unpaid bills and forgotten birthdays. Gerald nodded in approval, for the meal was perfectly balanced between nothing and everything, a culinary masterpiece that required no digestion, only a deep, existential sigh.
